title: Stem-and-Leaf Plots: Reading, Median, Range and Shape
seo_title: Year 7 Stem-and-Leaf Plot Worksheets: Reading Plots, Median, Mode, Range and Back-to-Back Plots (Free, Answer Key)

meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on stem-and-leaf plots for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7ST02): reading plots, median, mode, range and mean, building plots, shape, outliers and back-to-back plots. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Stem = tens digit, leaf = ones digit: 3 | 6 means 36.
key_sub: Count the leaves to find how many values there are, then count to the middle for the median.
body_html:
How it works

A stem-and-leaf plot shows every value of numerical data. The stem is usually the tens digit and the leaf is the ones digit, so 3 | 6 means 36. Always include a key, and write the leaves in order.

From an ordered plot you can read the smallest and largest values, count to the median, spot the mode and outliers, and see the shape: symmetrical, or skewed with a long tail.

Example

How many values are in the plot above?

Count the leaves.

Answer: 9

Example

What is the median?

9 values: the 5th value.

Answer: 23

Example

What is the range?

34 − 12.

Answer: 22

Common mistakes

  • Reading a leaf on its own: in 2 | 4 the value is 24, not 4.
  • Counting the stems instead of the leaves.
  • Finding the median without the leaves in order.
  • Leaving out repeated values: 23 and 23 need two leaves.

faq.q: How do you read a stem-and-leaf plot?
faq.a: Join each leaf to its stem using the key. If the key says 3 | 6 = 36, then a leaf of 2 on stem 4 means 42.

faq.q: How do you find the median from a stem-and-leaf plot?
faq.a: Count the leaves to find how many values there are, then count from the start to the middle value.

faq.q: What is a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot?
faq.a: Two data sets share the same stems: one set's leaves go to the right and the other's to the left, so they are easy to compare.
Most values are bunched at one end with a long tail at the other. A tail of high values is positively skewed.

items.q: How would you describe the shape of this distribution?
c: Positively skewed, with a long tail of high values
Negatively skewed, with a long tail of low values
Roughly symmetrical, with most values in the middle
Every value appears once with no pattern
items.e: The rows are short, long, short, so it is roughly symmetrical.

items.q: How would you describe the shape of this distribution?
c: Positively skewed, with a tail of high values
Negatively skewed, with a tail of low values
items.e: Most values are low, with a few much higher: positively skewed.

items.q: Which measure of centre best describes a typical value here?
c: The median, because the high values pull the mean up
The mean, because it uses every value
items.e: The tail of high values (and 45) pulls the mean up, so the median is more typical.

items.q: In the key 3 | 6 = 36, what does the 3 represent?
items.e: The stem is the tens digit and the leaf is the ones digit.

items.q: Why should the leaves in each row be written in order?
c: It does not matter at all
So you can read the median and other values easily
items.e: An ordered plot lets you count to the middle and read the smallest and largest values.

items.q: A stem-and-leaf plot has stems 1 to 5 and 18 leaves altogether. How many values does it show?
items.e: Every leaf is one value: 18.

items.q: What is one advantage of a stem-and-leaf plot over a column graph?
c: It can show categories like colours
You can still see every actual data value
items.e: A stem-and-leaf plot keeps the original numbers, so you can still see every value.

items.q: In a plot with key 2 | 3 = 2.3, what value does 4 | 7 show?
items.e: With this key the stem is the ones digit and the leaf is tenths: 4.7.

items.q: A row reads 6 | 0 0 4 9. Which values are in this row?
items.e: Each leaf joins the stem: 60, 60, 64 and 69.

items.q: Which data set is best shown in a stem-and-leaf plot?
c: The country each tourist came from
The type of pet each student owns
The ages of 25 people at a party
items.e: Stem-and-leaf plots are for numerical data such as ages.

items.q: A plot has rows 1 | 5 8, 2 | 0 3 3 7, 3 | 1 4. What is the mode?
items.e: The value 23 appears twice: 23.

items.q: A plot has rows 1 | 5 8, 2 | 0 3 3 7, 3 | 1 4. What is the median?
items.e: 8 values: halfway between the 4th (23) and 5th (23) is 23.

items.q: A plot has rows 1 | 5 8, 2 | 0 3 3 7, 3 | 1 4. What is the range?
Removing a very high outlier from a data set would…
items.e: A high outlier pulls the mean up, so removing it lowers the mean.

items.q: Two back-to-back plots have the same median, but one has a much larger range. What does this tell you?
c: Its data is more spread out
items.e: A larger range means the data is more spread out.
